title: Talking Keyboard — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Talking Keyboard's rich face: the instrument played from its own SFZ, the spoken-A bug heard and read one layer down, and the page's future variants rendered before anyone builds them. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.by: Web Audio · reads the build's SFZ
pieces.near: It also gave instant audible verification
pieces.title: 88 keys · four steps
pieces.caption: **The instrument, played from its own SFZ.** One key held, then one key's four voices by where you press, then all 88, and last a hidden mapping bug to find by ear. The page plays `talking_keyboard.sfz` itself, so a tap cuts the word the way the SFZ's `no_loop` and 50 ms release say it would; a switch plays on as `one_shot`. The test finds the claim holds for a bug that moves every name, and waits about thirty presses for one that swaps two keys.

pieces.title: three spellings of A · five steps
pieces.caption: **The bug only listening caught, played back.** A4 as it ships; the spec's “A four”, which the front end wrote as ɐ, the article; pass one's “ay”, written ˈaɪ; the build's seven-spelling audition, where ay, aye and ey come out as one file; and last a blind test of your ear, beside what the front end wrote for each before any sound existed and a vowel meter's reading of the sound. Renders made 2026-11-03 with the build's settings; every shipped file re-renders to within two 16-bit steps.

pieces.title: the next variant · four steps
pieces.caption: **The variants, rendered first.** Solfège through the build's English front end gets one syllable of seven right (do comes out “doo”, mi “my”, ti “tie”); respelt, all seven; the page's “Do quattro” in Italian, all seven; its “Do quatre” in French, six, with C handed to English and the language flags spoken. Last, the pitch-class variant: name the octave of a C with and without the octave word, beside the voice pitch, which stays near 200 Hz from C1 to C7.

pieces.title: velocity-as-language madlib · v2 mockup, 2026-05-04
pieces.caption: **A variant the list doesn't name, from the bundle.** A silent mockup from two days after the build: each key a word, the velocity layer picking the language (Latin, Japanese, English, French, German). No sound; its words are placeholders. Kept here as the record of a voice scheme that was sketched and not built.

offers.what: “Only listening caught it” is true of what was reviewed, the spec and the script, but the bug was written down one layer below them before any sound existed: kokoro-onnx 0.5.0’s front end (espeak-ng) turns “A four” into ɐ fˈɔːɹ (the article), “ay four” into ˈaɪ fˈɔːɹ, and “eigh four” into ˈeɪ fˈɔːɹ; it reads “A” alone as ˈeɪ, so the word after it is what makes A an article. A check that every A comes out as /ˈeɪ/ would have stopped both bad renders; it could not have chosen among ate, ace, “A.” and eigh, which all pass it, so the audition and the ear stay the last gate. Also measured: ay, aye and ey give the same phonemes and so the same audio, sample for sample. Suggest: “Only listening caught it, though the front end had already written it down: ɐ for A, ˈaɪ for ay.”

“Any mapping bug is obvious in the first second of play” holds for a bug that moves names across the whole map (an octave or semitone shift shows on the first key you check). It overstates two cases: a bug confined to a few keys shows only when you press one, and pressing distinct keys at random you first meet one of k bad keys on press (N+1)/(k+1), so about the 30th for a swapped pair (89/3 = 29.7; simulated 29.66); and a bug in the velocity split never shows in the names at all. Suggest: “any mapping bug is obvious the first time you press a key it touches.” The map itself checks clean: 352 regions, each naming its own key by generate.py’s naming, tiling velocity 1–127 in the four stated layers.

The solfège variant as written would hit the A lesson again: through the build’s en-us front end, 1 of 7 syllables comes out as meant (do → dˈuː, re → ɹˌiː, mi → mˈaɪ, sol → sˈɑːl, la → lˌæ, ti → tˈaɪ; only fa). Respelt (doe ray mee fah soh lah tee), 7 of 7. The page’s own “Do quattro” through the Italian front end in if_sara reads all 7; its “Do quatre” through the French front end in ff_siwis reads 6, and on do it switches to English and writes (en)dˈuː(fr), language flags that kokoro-onnx passes to the model as sounds (that render runs 1216 ms, the other six 811–896). Suggest a clause on the solfège line: each variant needs the audition gate, and a phoneme check before it.

The pitch-class variant loses positional verification entirely, not partly, for a reason the page doesn’t state: no sample is pitched to its key (every region’s pitch_keycenter is its own key, so nothing is retuned), and the voice speaks at 125 to 240 Hz across C1 to C7 in all four layers (at most ×1.23 within a layer) while the keys span ×64. With the octave word gone, seven Cs are one sound. This also bears on the first Open Question: the keyboard teaches the names of positions, not pitches by ear. Suggest a clause on the pitch-class line, and a note under Open Questions.

A build finding the 88-keys piece plays: talking_keyboard.sfz sets ampeg_attack=0.001 ampeg_release=0.05 in its group and no loop_mode, so by the SFZ spec it plays as no_loop, stopping 50 ms after the key comes up; a tap shorter than the word cuts it. BUILD.md lines 114–115 asked for no ampeg opcodes and one-shots. One opcode in the group, loop_mode=one_shot, would make a tap speak the whole name. Read from the spec, not tried in sforzando. The text could add “(hold the key: the SFZ is no_loop)” to the Format line, or nothing if the SFZ is fixed.

bf_emma is called a British female voice, and its timbre is, but generate.py (line 104) passes lang="en-us" for all four voices, so it is handed American phonemes: “F sharp five” reaches it as ˈɛf ʃˈɑːɹp fˈaɪv, r and all. Suggest “bf_emma’s British voice, speaking American phonemes”, or nothing.
